Given

\n\n

Buying price of refrigerator = ₹12,000

\n\n

Repair cost = ₹1,000

\n\n

Selling price = ₹15,000

\n\n

Concept:

\n\n

Gain = [(Selling Price - Total Cost Price)/Total Cost Price] ×  100

\n\n

Calculation:

\n\n

Total cost = Buying price + Repair cost

\n\n

₹12,000 + ₹1,000 = ₹13,000

\n\n

⇒ Gain = [(₹15,000 - ₹13,000) / ₹13,000] × 100

\n\n

⇒ 2000/13000 × 100 = 200/13% = \\(15\\frac{5}{13} \\)%

\n\n

Therefore,  His gain percentage is \\(15\\frac{5}{13} \\)%.TT

\n\n190:T30f8,\nदी गई जानकारी:

\n\n

रेफ्रिजरेटर का क्रय मूल्य = ₹ 12,000

\n\n

मरम्मत की लागत = ₹1,000

\n\n

विक्रय मूल्य = ₹ 15,000

\n\n

अवधारणा:

\n\n

लाभ प्रतिशत = [(विक्रय मूल्य - कुल क्रय मूल्य) / कुल क्रय मूल्य] × 100

\n\n

गणना:

\n\n

कुल लागत = क्रय मूल्य + मरम्मत लागत = ₹12,000 + ₹1,000 = ₹13,000

\n\n

⇒ लाभ प्रतिशत = [(₹15,000 - ₹13,000) / ₹13,000] ×  100

\n\n

⇒ 2000/13000 × 100 = 200/13% = \\(15\\frac{5}{13} \\)%

\n\n

अतः, उसका लाभ \\(15\\frac{5}{13} \\)% है।

"

Given

\n\n

Average of 9 numbers = 15

\n\n

Average of first five numbers = 13

\n\n

Average of last five numbers = 17

\n\n

Concept:

\n\n

Average = Sum of numbers/Number of numbers.

\n\n

Calculation:

\n\n

Sum of 9 num", "hn": "

दी गई जानकारी:

\n\n

9 संख्याओं का औसत = 15

\n\n

पहली पाँच संख्याओं का औसत = 13

\n\n

अंतिम पाँच संख्याओं का औसत = 17

\n\n

अवधारणा:

\n\n

औसत = संख्याओं का योग/संख्याओं की संख्या

\n\n

गणना:

\n\n

9 संख्याओं का योग = 9 ×  15 = 135

\n\n

⇒ पहली पाँच संख्याओं का योग = 5 ×  13 = 65

\n\n

⇒ अंतिम पाँच संख्याओं का योग = 5 × 17 = 85

\n\n

\n\n

\n\n
 
\n\n
The word 'Universal', corresponds closely with 'omnipresent' as it also implies something that is common to or affects all. The Hindi meaning for Universal is 'सार्वभौमिक'. For instance: Mathematics is a universal subject because it remains the same no matter where it's taught.

\n\n

Key points:
\n\n
 
\n\n
Simple past tense is used to talk about a completed action at a certain time in the past. It only requires the past form of the verb.
\n\n
The sentence "I gave some of the chocolates to my younger sister" uses the verb 'gave' which is the simple past form of 'give' indicating a completed action.
\n\n
The other options involve past continuous, past perfect continuous, and past perfect tenses which do not fit the requirement for simple past tense.
\n\n
Additionally, Simple past tense does not use auxiliary verbs which we see present in the options a), b), c. Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 2: I gave some of the chocolates to my younger sister.'
\n\n
Additional Information:
\n\n
 
\n\n
Option A ("I was giving some of the chocolates to my younger sister") is in the past continuous tense. It denotes an ongoing action in the past.
\n\n
Option B ("I had been giving some of the chocolates to my younger sister") is in the past perfect continuous tense. It refers to an action that started in the past and continued up until another time in the past.
\n\n
Option C ("I had given some of the chocolates to my younger sister") is in the past perfect tense. It is used for an action completed before another point in the past.
